2303:
** θεῖον**,
**A**_Epic dialect_ **θέειον** (in {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.493}} θήϊον), τό, **brimstone**, used to fumigate and purify, δέπας.. ἐκάθηρε θεείῳ {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 16.228; οἶσε θέειον.., κακῶν ἄκος 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 22.481}}; δεινὴ δὲ θεείου γίγνεται ὀδμή, from a thunderbolt, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.415}}; ἐν δὲ θεείου πλῆτο, of a ship struck by lightning, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 12.417}}; ἐμβαλόντες πῦρ ξὺν θ. {{LXX+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.77, compare 4.100; Κύριος ἔβρεξεν ἐπὶ Σόδομα καὶ Γόμορρα θ. καὶ πῦρ LXX.Gen.19.24}}; as a natural product, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “Aër.” 7, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.21, 143, 5th-4th c.BC: Timaeus Locrus Philosophus 99c; θ. ἄπυρον 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 12.903}}; opposed to πεπυρωμένον, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 5.107}}; compare θεάφιον, θέαφος. (Perh. _cognate_ with θύω, θυμιάω, Latin _suffire._)
2309:
** θέλω**,
see at {ἐθέλω} and add ὅστις ἂν θέλῃ {{Refs|“IG” 12.49.12; ἐὰν δέ τις θέλῃ [prev. work]6.106; ἐάν τις μὴ θέλῃ [prev. work]40.27.}}
2313:
** θεομᾰχ-έω**,
**fight against God** or **the gods**, {{LXX+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 45, +others, “IA” 1408; μὴ θεομάχει 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 187, compare 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἐπιστολαί” 14, LXX.2Mac.7.19, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.168c, 2nd c.AD: Arrianus Historicus “Epicteti Dissertationes” 3.24.24.}}
2314:
** θεομά?~Xχ-ος**, ον,
**fighting against God**, Γίγαντες {{NT+2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Scymnus Geographus 637, cf. NT.Act.5.39, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “JTr.” 45, 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 331.12.}}
2315:
** θεό-πνευ-στος**, ον,
**inspired of God**, σοφίη {{NT+1st c.AD+|1st c.AD(?): Pseudo-Phocylidea 129; ὄνειροι 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.904f; πᾶσα γραφή NT.2Tim.3.16; δημιούργημα 2nd c.AD: Vettius Valens Astrologus 330.19.}}
2317:
** θεοσέβ-εια**, ἡ,
**service** or **fear of God, religiousness**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.6.26, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epinomis” 985c, 990a, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “in Hes.” 46, 4th c.AD: Iamblichus Philosophus “Protrepticus” 20.}}
2318:
** θεοσεβ-ής**, ές,
**fearing God, religious**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.86, 2.37, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 260 (_superlative_), 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 394d, +others; θ. μέλος 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 897 (Lyric poetry); τὸ θεοσεβές 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epinomis” 977e}}. _adverb_ **-βῶς**{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.58.}}
2319:
** θεο-στῠγής**, ές,
**hated of the gods**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Troades” 1213, “Cyc.” 602, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 1.21}}; **hated of God,** {{NT|NT.Rom.1.30}} (where some take it _active_, **hating God**).
2320:
** θεότης**, ητος, ἡ,
**divinity, divine nature,** {{NT+1st c.AD+|NT.Col.2.9, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.359d, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Icar.” 9, etc.}}; διὰ θεότητα **for religious reasons**, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Heliodorus Medicus cited in 4th c.AD: Oribasius Medicus 50.7.1.}}

2365:
** θῠγάτρ-ιον**, τό,
_diminutive_ of θυγάτηρ, **little daughter** or **girl**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Strattis Comicus 63, 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 428, “PPetr.” 3p.155 (3rd c.BC), 3rd c.BC: Macho Comicus cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 13.581c, “Comica Adespota” 14.19 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, “SIG” 364.55 (Ephesus, 3rd c.BC), 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Antonius” 33, 4th c.AD: Julianus Imperator “Orationes” 7.226b.}}
2366:
** θύελλ-α** [ῠ], ἡ,
(θύω, compare ἄελλα from ἄημι) **hurricane, squall** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|compare (4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 395a6), κακὴ ἀνέμοιο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.346, +others}}; μισγομένων ἀνέμων.. θ. {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.317}}; πυρός τ᾽ ὀλοοῖο θύελλαι, probably **thunderstorms**, {{Refs|12.68; κούρας ἀνέλοντο θ. 20.66}}; τοὺς δ᾽ αἶψ᾽ ἁρπάξασα φέρεν πόντονδε θ{{Refs 5th c.BC+|. 10.48, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 1151}}; ποντία θ. {{Refs 8th c.BC+|[prev. author] “OC” 1660; in similes, φλογὶ ἶσοι ἠὲ θυέλλῃ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.39}}; ἴκελοι πυρὶ ἠὲ θ. {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Scutum Herculis” 345: _metaphorically_, ἄτης θύελλαι (nisi to be read θυηλαί, which see) 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 819}}; ὀχλικὴ θ. {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.184S.}}
2367:
** θύϊνος** [ῠ], η, ον,
**of the tree** θύον (which see), δένδρα, ξύλον, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 4.6.2, variant in 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1.22}}; **made of this wood**, {{NT+3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC(?): Callixinus Historicus 1, NT.Rev.18.12.}}
2377:
** θῠρωρ-ός**,
{{Refs 5th c.AD+|5th c.AD: Cypria}} **θυραϝωρός** uncertain in {{Refs|“Inscription Cyprian dialect” 215 H}}., _Epic dialect_ **θυραωρός** (which see), ὁ, ἡ:— **door-keeper, porter**, {{NT+7th c.BC+|7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 98, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.120, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 565, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 62c, NT.Mark.13.34, “BGU” 1061.10 (1st c.AD), 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Vit.Auct.” 7, etc.}}:—also **θυρουρός** {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“PCair.Zen.” 292.76 (3rd c.BC), “PRyl.” 136.6 (1st c.AD), “IG” 3.1137 (2nd c.AD), “PFlor.” 71.380 (4th c.AD)}}. (From θυρα-**ho**ρϝος, compare οὖρος, ἐρύω (B): connected with ὠρέω by {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Cornutus Philosophus “de Natura Deorum” 1.)}}
2379:
** θῠσι-αστήριον**, τό,
**altar**,{{LXX+NT+1st c.AD+|LXX.Exo.27.1, +others, NT.Matt.23.18, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 8.4.1, “Codex Justinianus [4th-6th c.AD]” 1.12.3.2.}}

2384:
**Ἰακώβ**, ὁ indecl. (Heb. יַעֲקֹב),
**Jacob**;
1. **The patriarch**: Mat.1:2 8:11, Jhn.4:5-6, Act.7:8, al; as in _Heb._ (cf. Num.23:7, Isa.41:8, Sir.23:12, al.), of his descendants, Rom.11:26 (LXX).
2. **The father-in-law of Mary**: Mat.1:15-16 (on the form as distinct from that of the next word, see Deiss., BS, 3161)
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)
2385:
**Ἰάκωβος**, -ου, ὁ (Heb., see previous word)
**James**;
1. **Son of Zebedee**: Mat.4:21, Mrk.1:19, 29, Act.1:13 12:2, al.
2. **Son of Alphæus**: Mat.10:3, Mrk.2:14, al.; commonly identified with Ἰ. ὁ μικρός, James the little, son of Mary (see: Μαρία, 3; Κλωπᾶς), Mat.27:56, Mrk.15:40 16:1 (cf. Jhn.19:25).
3. **The Lord's brother **(see: ἀδελφός): Mat.13:55, Mrk.6:3, Act.12:17, al., 1Co.15:7 (probably), Gal.1:19 2:9, 12, Jas.1:1, Ju 1.
4. **The father of the apostle, Ἰούδας Ἰακώβου**: Luk.6:16, Act.1:13
(From Abbott-Smith. LSJ has no entry)

2396:
** ἴδε**
**A** (_Attic dialect_ ἰδέ Hdn.Gr.1.431), _aorist 2_ _imperative_ of εἶδον, **behold**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.179, etc.: followed by ὅτι.., 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 72a}}; used by Trag. in Lyric poetry, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Supplices” 350, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 222, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 1541.}}
